title: Evidence collector rate limits and priority queueing patterns
summary: Working spec for soft/hard rate limits, multi-priority queueing, and backpressure behaviors for evidence collectors that feed the SIEM export pipeline. Includes operational knobs, auth rotation notes, and a lightweight signed-envelope export mode for downstream archive and forensics.
goals: Ensure collectors can operate across varied customer environments (VPC, on-prem, hosted) without causing downstream SIEM overloads.
Define priority classes so high-trust control evidence (RBAC changes, attestations) is exported ahead of lower-value telemetry while preserving fairness.
Provide concrete failure/slowdown modes and mitigation steps for on-call teams.
Standardize a compact envelope format for exports that preserves provenance and supports rehydration for audits.
background: We currently observe bursty audit streams from some customers leading to SIEM ingestion spikes. Existing collectors either drop or buffer arbitrarily, causing gaps in audit chains. This doc sketches a pragmatic rate-limit + priority queue design tailored to evidence (not generic logs) and aligns operator expectations with alerting and recovery steps.
scope: Applies to all collector variants (edge-side agent, sidecar, lambda harvesters).
Focus on emit-side controls (before network/send) — not downstream SIEM ingestion throttles.
Does not redesign the evidence schema; assumes minimal envelope fields (id, ts, origin, signature, type, payload_ref).
constraints: Collectors run in constrained environments (1-2 CPU, limited RAM) on customer infra — computational overhead must be minimal.
Cannot rely on central coordination for short-term burst smoothing (network partitions).
Must support stateless restart without losing priority semantics where possible.
design_overview: Each collector implements a small local queueing layer with three priority bands (P0, P1, P2). A token-bucket rate limiter governs egress per destination (e.g., siem-ingest.example.com). If the bucket is empty, P0 items are allowed a small emergency bypass budget; P1/P2 are buffered to disk-based spillover or dropped according to policy. Export envelopes are serialized compactly (newline-delimited JSON) and signed/HMACed before send. Metadata about dropped/held events is emitted to a local health endpoint for scraping.
queueing_policy: Priority bands: P0 = control-evidence (RBAC, attestations, chain-of-custody), P1 = user-audit (login, config changes), P2 = noisy telemetry/metrics exports.
In-memory queue depth defaults: P0=500, P1=2000, P2=5000. These are tunable by config and scaled down for tiny agents.
Spillover: when in-memory queue >75% full, move oldest P2 items to compressed local spill file (gzip newline JSON).
Eviction: P2 oldest-first eviction when total disk + mem > configured cap. P1 is only evicted as last resort after disk saturates. P0 never evicted unless explicitly operator-forced.
rate_limit_strategy: Token-bucket per-destination with configurable capacity and refill rate. Default: capacity=1000 tokens, refill=100 tokens/sec (one token ~= one 1KB envelope).
Burst window: allow short bursts up to 3x capacity if a signed emergency token (rotatable key) is presented by control-plane for prioritized exports.
Backpressure signal: when limiter is <10% tokens, collector marks health endpoint status=degraded and sets metric collector.rate_limited=true for scraping.
Soft vs hard limits: soft limits trigger buffering; hard limits trigger policy-driven drops and emit a 'dropped-summary' control envelope (aggregated counts per minute).
priority_keying: Default keying rules: RBAC-change events (type=rback_change|rbac_v2) => P0; attestation/chain-of-custody => P0; API-key rotations and KMS events => P0.
Configurable overrides: customers can add regex matchers on event.path or event.meta to bump/demote priority locally.
Sticky ordering: within the same priority and same origin-session, preserve FIFO ordering to maintain causality where possible.
auth_and_rotation: Collectors authenticate to our export endpoint using short-lived client certs or signed JWTs depending on deployment mode.
Rotate HMAC keys every 24 hours by default; allow rotation window of 72 hours for staggered fleets. Collectors must accept previous key for replay verification for the window period.
Emergency key/bypass: control-plane can issue single-use bypass tokens (JWT with 'bypass':true) to drain critical queues during incidents. Tokens logged centrally for audit.
export_format_and_siem: Envelope fields (required): id, ts_utc, origin_id, origin_type, priority, type, payload_ref (s3:// or inline base64), signature_scheme, signature, schema_version.
Compact export is newline-delimited JSON. For large payloads (>128KB) collectors upload object to configured archive (S3-compatible) and put payload_ref rather than inline payload.
SIEM shim: a lightweight adapter handles mapping envelope.type -> siem index/stream. Adapter includes dedupe by id and will accept resends with identical id up to 7 days (idempotency window).
Support for alternate sinks: kube event API, syslog gateway, and direct Kafka topic 'evidence-archive' for high-throughput customers.
data_retention_and_ttl: Local spill files TTL: default 72 hours. Older spillovers are purged by background sweeper.
Signed envelope TTL: included ts_utc + ttl_seconds field. Downstream systems must respect and honor TTL for archival vs delete decisions.
Reingestion window: collector exposes reingest endpoint for spill files within 14 days if operator requests backfill.
error_modes_and_retries: Network transient: exponential backoff with jitter (base 100ms, max 30s) up to 12 retries, then escalate to spillover to disk and mark health degraded.
Permanent 4xx: drop if unrecoverable (e.g., schema mismatch). Emit a control-envelope describing last error and sample payload id for offline analysis.
Partial success: if batch endpoint returns per-item status, mark successes as sent, retry failures according to retry policy. No duplicate acking of successful ids.
Corruption detection: signature verification failure triggers quarantine of item to quarantine directory and alert to security triage.
rollout_checklist: Feature-flag gating in edge agents for initial 10% of fleet.
Simulated burst tests using local load harness (script: tools/collector-load-test.sh).
Enable verbose audit logging for first 72 hours after rollout to capture misclassification of priorities.
Ops runbook updated with runbook id RR-collector-queue-01 and escalation matrix.
Post-rollout retrospective scheduled (2 weeks after rollout) to capture tuning values.
migration_and_backfill_plan: When enabling new priority mapping, run a dry-run mode where events are tagged with new_priority but still sent with old behaviour for 48 hours, log mismatches.
Backfill spilled events: provide a controlled reingest CLI (reingest-spill --limit N --priority X) that honors current rate limits and writes to 'reingest' topic with an audit header.
Record mapping changes in a changelog stored in S3 prefix s3://redwood-evidence-changelog/priority-mappings/ for auditors.
open_questions: What should default capacity be for very small on-prem appliances (1 vCPU)? Proposal: scale down capacities by factor 10.
Do we support encrypt-then-sign for large payloads or rely on transport TLS + HMAC? Need security signoff.
Should the control-plane have the ability to remotely purge local spill files for legal/compliance requests? Privacy/legal input required.
notes_to_self: Next steps: prototype limiter in Go runtime, get perf numbers, draft RFC for security review (owner: evelyn). Put validation tests behind CI gate and link to JIRA-SEC-2141.
operational_tips: Use metrics to tune refill rate; watch collector.rate_limited.total spike as early indicator.
During incident, issue single-use bypass token and monitor for duplicate ids downstream.
If spill files accumulate, check network egress and DNS resolution to siem endpoint before raising infrastructure pager.
